name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 500 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 52% more than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 500 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 52 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Militants killed three Meitei men in Manipur and their bodies were placed outside the chief minister's residence, prompting protests. An IED blast in Manipur injured three CRPF personnel, and militants also killed three villagers in a separate ambush. In Kashmir, a cabinet expansion is set to occur after the lieutenant governor returns, while curfews were imposed in four northern communes following protest violence. The Cockroach Janta party leader was arrested amid a nationwide crackdown on protests. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantene drepte tre Meitei-menn i Manipur, og likene deres ble plassert utenfor statsministerens residens, noe som førte til protester. En IED-eksplosjon i Manipur såret tre CRPF-personell, og militantene drepte også tre landsbyboere i et separat bakholdsangrep. I Kashmir vil en kabinettutvidelse finne sted etter at lederen for delstaten vender tilbake, mens portforbud ble innført i fire nordlige kommuner etter protestvold. Leder for Cockroach Janta-partiet ble arrestert i en landsomfattende nedslag på protester. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
